cards.explanation: The answer is False, friends. The message says the king will NOT recover. Isaiah, the prophet, tells him, “Put your house in order, for you are about to die; you will not recover.” (Isaiah 38:1) I think this one hurts.

The answer is to put his house in order, friends. The LORD's message says, “Put your house in order, for you are about to die…” (Isaiah 38:1) That's a plain instruction for a plain, heavy moment. I think it's one of those lines that makes a whole room go quiet.

The answer is how he has walked faithfully before the LORD, friends. Hezekiah, king of Judah, prays, “Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before You faithfully and with wholehearted devotion…” (Isaiah 38:3) He doesn't bring a list of his accomplishments. He brings how he has walked with the LORD.
The answer is weeps, friends. After he prays, the text says, “And Hezekiah wept bitterly.” (Isaiah 38:3) That's no polite sniffle. It's a king with his face to the wall and nothing held back.
The answer is David, friends. The LORD tells Isaiah to say He is “…the God of your father David…” (Isaiah 38:5) So the message comes from the LORD, and He names David right there.

The answer is fifteen, friends. The LORD says, “Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.” (Isaiah 38:5) The man was told he'd die, and now he's got fifteen years. That's a plot twist I'd happily read twice.

The answer is Assyria, friends. The LORD says, “And I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria.” (Isaiah 38:6) That's a promise about the king's life and about his whole city. The LORD adds, “I will defend this city.” (Isaiah 38:6)

The answer is that the shadow goes back ten steps, friends. The LORD says, “I will make the sun’s shadow that falls on the stairway of Ahaz go back ten steps.” (Isaiah 38:8) And then the text tells us, “So the sunlight went back the ten steps it had descended.” I've watched a lot of timers tick down, and I have NEVER seen one go back ten.

The answer is that he'd never again see the LORD, friends. Hezekiah says, “I will never again see the LORD, even the LORD, in the land of the living…” (Isaiah 38:11) He says the name twice, and I think that shows how much it weighed on him.

The answer is loom, friends. Hezekiah says, “I have rolled up my life like a weaver; He cuts me off from the loom…” (Isaiah 38:12) He's picturing a weaver who's finished mid-thread. A picture like that says a lot with very few words.

The answer is security, friends. Hezekiah prays, “O Lord, I am oppressed; be my security.” (Isaiah 38:14) He's weak and worn out, and his eyes are growing weak as he looks upward. So he asks the Lord to stand behind him.

The answer is True, friends. Hezekiah says, “I will walk slowly all my years because of the anguish of my soul.” (Isaiah 38:15) I think the hard days stayed with him, and I know a little about that myself.
The answer is False, friends. Hezekiah says, “Surely for my own welfare I had such great anguish…” (Isaiah 38:17) He doesn't call it for nothing. He looks back and says it was for his welfare.

The answer is behind His back, friends. Hezekiah says to the Lord, “…You have cast all my sins behind Your back.” (Isaiah 38:17) All of them, not just the small ones. That's a thing worth smiling about.

The answer is only the living, friends. Hezekiah says, “The living, only the living, can thank You, as I do today…” (Isaiah 38:19) He says "the living" twice, and I bet he's still amazed he's one of them.

The answer is faithfulness, friends. Hezekiah says, “fathers will tell their children about Your faithfulness.” (Isaiah 38:19) He's already thinking about the next generation. I'd pass that along too.

The answer is a lump of pressed figs, friends. The text says, “Prepare a lump of pressed figs and apply it to the boil, and he will recover.” (Isaiah 38:21) That's Isaiah's exact instruction. Those figs were meant for Hezekiah's boil. Figs, friends. Just figs.

The answer is True, friends. The text says Hezekiah had asked, “What will be the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?” (Isaiah 38:22) I think a man who had been that sick would be eager to go up to the house of the LORD.
